justification_text:
My point estimates reflect a modestly bullish baseline for what appears to be an asset trading near the 378–380 range. At the one-day horizon, I anchored close to the last observed price around 378.5, expecting minimal drift given that short-term price movements in liquid markets tend to mean-revert or continue with low magnitude. The slight upward drift in the one-week and one-month estimates reflects a gentle positive trend assumption, consistent with either a broadly risk-on environment or an asset with modest positive carry or momentum. I did not embed a strong directional view; rather, the small upward slope in point estimates reflects a slight bias toward continuation of recent price action rather than any fundamental catalyst I was highly confident about.

The confidence interval widths expand naturally with time horizon, which is a standard reflection of uncertainty compounding over longer periods. At one day, the 90% interval of roughly plus or minus 10 points reflects typical daily volatility for a moderately volatile instrument. At one week, the interval widens to about plus or minus 22 points, and at one month it reaches roughly plus or minus 42 points, consistent with volatility scaling approximately with the square root of time. These widths also bake in uncertainty about the volatility regime itself — whether realized volatility will be calm or elevated — which adds additional spread beyond pure statistical scaling.

Specific risks that could push outcomes outside my stated intervals include sharp macroeconomic surprises such as an unexpected central bank policy shift, inflation data significantly off consensus, or a sudden deterioration in financial conditions that triggers risk-off selling. On the upside, a strong positive catalyst — such as better-than-expected economic data, a geopolitical resolution, or a short squeeze — could push prices well above 425 on the monthly horizon. Liquidity events, flash crashes, or correlated deleveraging across asset classes could similarly drive the price below 340 in a tail scenario. My intervals are intentionally wide enough to capture most plausible outcomes but are not designed to cover genuine black swan events, which by definition carry meaningful probability of breaching any pre-specified range.
